title: First Cable That Closes a Loop
statement:
Cables are laid between `nodes` computers numbered `0` to `nodes - 1`, one at a time, in the order of `edges`. Each `[a, b]` joins computers `a` and `b` in both directions.

Return the **position** (counting from `0`) of the first cable that joins two computers that were **already connected**, directly or through other cables, so it closes a loop. Return `-1` if no cable does.
constraints: each edge has two different numbers in 0..nodes-1; the same pair may appear more than once

examples.explanation: After cables 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, computers 0 and 3 are already connected, so the 4th cable (position 3) closes a loop.
Each cable joins two separate groups, so there is no loop.

hints.nudge: Before adding a cable, ask one question: are its two ends ALREADY in the same group of connected computers?
hints.pattern: Union-Find (disjoint set union): keep the connected groups, find each computer's group leader, and merge groups when a cable joins them.
hints.pseudocode:
parent[i] = i for every computer
find(x): follow parent until a leader (shorten the path as you go)
for each cable (a, b) at position i:
  if find(a) == find(b): return i
  parent[find(a)] = find(b)
return -1
hints.walkthrough: Checking, for every new cable, whether its ends are already connected by searching the existing network costs O(V + E) each time, O(E * (V + E)) overall. Union-Find answers 'are a and b connected?' almost instantly. Give every computer its own group leader. To find the group of x, follow the parent links until a computer that is its own parent; shortening the links on the way (path compression) keeps the chains short. For each cable in order: find the leaders of both ends; if they are the same, the ends are already connected and this cable closes a loop, so return its position; otherwise merge by making one leader the parent of the other. If no cable ever closes a loop, return -1. Practically O(E).
